Do you think I'd actually be able to spot it?

Probably not—at least not easily.

The Moon is geometrically above the horizon and reasonably far from the Sun (about 99°), so it is not hidden by glare near the Sun. But at 09:40 in clear, bright Lagos daylight, a 58%-illuminated Moon at only about 31° altitude will have very low contrast against the bright blue sky.

A practiced observer who knows its exact position and has excellent eyesight might be able to pick it out, especially if the sky is exceptionally transparent and they use a building or hand to block distracting light. But for an ordinary unaided observer, even knowing roughly where to look, it would likely be difficult and quite possible not to see it at all.

So if it would be a relief for it not to be visible: you should not expect it to be conspicuous or readily noticeable.
